_notes.RemoteGrantRegistry.ts budget 26, messen: Owner permission 2026-11-28 (TL-D11): 4-29 approves one grant from Telegram or Bale with the manager's own time. The registry took min(policy, computer duration), so a time above the computer setting was cut; an optional exact flag on that one panel grant (4 lines; only the bot's custom time sets it; the phone and the "same as the computer" button are unchanged) keeps the chosen 1-1000 minutes, past 60 minutes with the 4-28 renewal. messengerRuntime.ts passes the minutes field into the BOT_DECISION access row (1 line).
_notes.tickets.ts (batch 3): Owner permission 2026-11-28 (TL-D12): 4-31 keeps the use count of a repeatable action on the computer, on the one-time ticket itself (uses and uses left; each use takes one and tells a host listener, which writes the "use n of m" access row); a multi-use ticket lasts until its uses run out or the end of the "money and sensitive" remote duration, at most 1000 minutes; close all, P1 and P2 clear it like any ticket. +32/-5 lines. The hub policy shape is untouched.
_notes.gate.ts, scheduledGrantsRuntime.ts (batc: Owner permission 2026-11-28 (TL-D13): 4-47 (with 4-13) makes a scheduled grant cover several modules and action locks, from a first day to a last day with the same daily hours, for everyone or for one employee. A ticked action lock must pass the gate as often as needed inside those hours, so gate.ts (outside the batch-3 list) lets an action pass without using a ticket while the scheduler keeps it open (5 changed lines: the import, takeTickets twice and the gateSession condition; the method recorded is the existing SCHEDULED_GRANT). The employee check needs who holds the register; scheduledGrantsRuntime.ts (also outside the list) reads it without writing: the custodian of the active custody segment (ACTIVE or HANDOVER_PENDING, custodian equal to the shift user) and the active staff list, as two injected dependencies (+11/-1). The nine irreversible actions are not in the list (owner answer exclude), and the test lines changed are plan1405-scheduled-grants.mjs 6, 52, 54 and 57 (owner answer yes-all).
_notes.messengerEngine.ts, messengerIpc.ts (bat: Owner permission 2026-11-28 (TL-D15): 4-12 sends the five new one-time codes to Telegram and Bale. The direct send and the new recipient tick can only live in messengerEngine.ts (bot API, settings and the recipient list; +41/-3), and the tick is saved through the existing recipient-update channel in messengerIpc.ts (same typed manager password; +9), which also hands the sender to lockIpc.ts. Both files were outside the batch-3 list (the architecture listed only oneTimeCodes.ts, lockIpc.ts, MessengerSettings.tsx and messengerTypes.ts). The codes stay in memory: no queue, no file (not even queue stats), no history row and no event; a failed send is not retried.
